lead: Bought bread, bakery goods, biscuits, chocolate, sweets, savoury snacks, snack bars and ice cream, organised by product kind, then named styles, makers and quality grades; dishes and recipes live in the Culinary Taxonomy.
ax: What kind of bought food is it: bread or baked goods, biscuits and crackers, chocolate, sweets, savoury snacks, snack nuts and bars, or ice cream?
key: 1. Is it a loaf, roll, flatbread, pastry or cake sold fresh or packaged from a bakery? → Bread & bakery
2. Is it a dry baked biscuit, cookie or cracker? → Biscuits & crackers
3. Is it chocolate itself, a chocolate piece or box, a chocolate countline or a seasonal chocolate shape? → Chocolate
4. Is it a sugar sweet, a gum, or a traditional nut, milk, syrup or sesame confection? → Sweets & confectionery
5. Is it a crisp, puffed or fried savoury snack eaten from the packet? → Crisps & savoury snacks
6. Is it a nut, seed, trail mix or a cereal, fruit or protein bar? → Snack nuts & bars
7. Is it frozen and eaten as ice cream, ice lolly or frozen dessert? → Ice cream

Precedence: a chocolate-coated biscuit is a biscuit (step 2) unless sold as a countline; a doughnut or cake is bakery (step 1) even when iced; a plain bag of nuts is step 6, a chocolate-coated nut is step 3; ice cream cake is step 7.

depts.t: Bread, pastry and cake bought from a baker or shop, fresh or packaged, listed by brand and market, then by the forms they come in; a dry biscuit or cracker → Biscuits & crackers; a chocolate bar → Chocolate; a dish made from bread belongs in the Culinary Taxonomy.
depts.ax: Who makes the loaf: a global bakery group, a national champion, an independent or a craft bakery; and what form does it take?
depts.note: Brands sit under the product they are best known for (Warburtons in Sliced & tin loaf); protected names (Pane di Altamura, Aachener Printen, Pastel de Tentúgal) sit in their product kinds; generic forms stay kinds and link to the Culinary Taxonomy. The tier breakdown is on the market view.
